title: Porting a Fortran plasma simulation to Exascale on AMD GPUs using both OpenMP and Kokkos
problem: Porting legacy Fortran HPC codes to GPU requires significant effort. OpenMP offloading provides good speedups for most code but becomes bottleneck on performance-critical components.
motivation: Demonstrate practical porting strategy for petascale Fortran codes to exascale GPU systems using hybrid approaches and portability frameworks.
method: The researchers took a two-part approach to moving Gysela (a turbulence simulation code) to GPU: first, they used OpenMP offloading (a standard technique that tells the compiler to run code on the GPU) across most of the code for broad coverage. Then, for the performance-critical collision operator—the part where the simulation spent most of its time—they rewrote that section in Kokkos (a C++ library designed to write code once but run efficiently on different hardware). They tested this on AMD hardware including the Genoa CPU, MI250X GPU, and MI300A APU (an all-in-one processor combining CPU and GPU) on the Adastra supercomputer.
key_novelty: The core finding is that you can efficiently port legacy Fortran code to GPU by first using OpenMP offloading for broad coverage, then surgically rewriting only the performance-critical collision operator in Kokkos.
contributions: OpenMP offloading porting strategy with speedups 1-12.5x
Identification of collision operator as bottleneck
Comparative benchmarking across CPU, GPU, APU architectures
Practical guidance for porting legacy Fortran codes
key_insights: OpenMP effective for most code except collision operator
Each framework suitable for different code patterns
limitations: Abstract does not provide specific KoLiOp speedup numbers. Limited comparison with other porting approaches.
primary_theme: Hybrid GPU Porting Strategy for Plasma Simulation
